skill.name: env-config
skill.description: Environment configuration and secrets management guidance for Python projects using UV. It covers .env files, environment variables, encrypted secrets, validation, multi-environment setups, and safer configuration workflows.
skill.summary: Manage Python environment configuration, .env files, and secrets with UV-focused guidance.
skill.author: AutumnsGrove

security_audit.summary: The skill is legitimate environment and secrets-management documentation, but it includes security-sensitive helper behavior and repeated pipe-to-shell installer recommendations. Most static matches are placeholders or expected .env guidance, while confirmed issues focus on unverified installer execution and possible disclosure of local secret values. Static review was capped at 400/653 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 253 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Remote installer scripts are piped directly into the shell.
remediation.suggestion: Replace pipe-to-shell commands with package-manager installation, checksum verification, or a download-then-inspect workflow.

remediation.issue: Environment comparison output can reveal secret value prefixes.
remediation.suggestion: Redact values for keys containing KEY, SECRET, PASSWORD, TOKEN, URL, or DATABASE before printing diffs.

remediation.issue: Decryption without an output path prints full secrets to stdout.
remediation.suggestion: Require an explicit output path or print only key names and metadata unless a user confirms secret display.

remediation.issue: Examples include printing database URLs and secret-related configuration.
remediation.suggestion: Change examples to print presence, validation status, or redacted values instead of raw configuration values.

semantic_findings.title: Sensitive Environment Values Printed During Comparison
semantic_findings.description: The helper prints prefixes of values from compared environment files. Environment values can include API keys, passwords, tokens, and database URLs, so comparison output can disclose secrets in logs or terminals.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The print_env_diff function directly prints key/value differences from .env files. Values are truncated but still may reveal enough of a secret to be sensitive.

semantic_findings.title: Decrypted Secrets Printed To Standard Output
semantic_findings.description: When decrypting without an output file, the CLI prints the full decrypted secrets JSON to standard output. This can leak secrets into shell history, terminal scrollback, or CI logs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The decrypt command loads decrypted secrets and prints json.dumps(secrets) when no output path is supplied. That is direct disclosure of secret material.

content.value_statement: Python projects often leak secrets or drift across development, staging, and production. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured guidance for safer .env files, validation, and secret handling.
actual_capabilities: Guides setup of UV-based Python projects with environment configuration files.
Explains .env templates, .gitignore entries, and variable naming conventions.
Provides helper script commands for validating, comparing, merging, and templating env files.
Describes optional encryption and decryption workflows for local secrets files.
Includes testing, troubleshooting, and cloud secret manager reference patterns.
limitations: It does not integrate directly with a live cloud secret manager without user implementation.
The included helper script can read and print local configuration values if used carelessly.
The documentation includes pipe-to-shell UV install commands that require safer replacement.
Examples use placeholders and must be adapted before production use.

use_cases.title: Bootstrap secure Python project configuration
use_cases.description: Create a repeatable UV project setup with .env templates, validation, and documented required variables.

use_cases.title: Standardize deployment environment files
use_cases.description: Compare development, staging, and production variables to reduce drift before release.

use_cases.title: Audit secret handling practices
use_cases.description: Review a project for committed secrets, weak placeholders, missing .gitignore rules, and unsafe logging patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic env template
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new Python project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the env-config skill to design a simple .env.template for my Python app. Include app settings, database settings, and API key placeholders without real secrets.

prompt_templates.title: Validate an existing configuration plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Check required variables and unsafe defaults.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the env-config skill to review my planned environment variables. Identify missing required values, unsafe defaults, and which files should be committed or ignored.

prompt_templates.title: Plan multi-environment configuration
prompt_templates.scenario: Separate local, staging, and production settings.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the env-config skill to design development, staging, and production environment files for a UV Python service. Show what belongs in each file and how to avoid secret drift.

prompt_templates.title: Audit secrets workflow before release
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the env-config skill to audit my Python service configuration workflow before production. Check .gitignore coverage, secret rotation, logging risks, validation, and deployment injection patterns.

output_examples.input: Set up configuration for a new UV Python API.
output: A recommended file layout for templates and local secrets.
A list of required environment variables by category.
Commands for installing dotenv and validation dependencies.
A warning about values that must not be committed.
A checklist for validation before startup.
Suggestions for runtime secret injection and rotation.

output_examples.input: Troubleshoot why variables are not loading.
output: A sequence of checks for file location, syntax, working directory, and dotenv loading order.
Safer debug guidance that avoids printing secret values.

best_practices: Commit templates and documentation, not real .env files or secrets files.
Validate required variables at startup and fail closed when production secrets are missing.
Redact sensitive values before logging, comparing, or sharing configuration output.
anti_patterns: Piping remote installer scripts directly into a shell without verification.
Printing decrypted secrets, database URLs, or API keys during debugging.
Copying production .env files into images or source control.

faq.question: Does this skill store or manage my real secrets?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and helper scripts. You decide which local files or secret managers to use.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code for environment configuration tasks.

faq.question: Is the included encryption a full enterprise secret management system?
faq.answer: No. It is a local encryption utility. Production systems should prefer managed secret stores when available.

faq.question: Should .env.production be committed?
faq.answer: No. Production files usually contain sensitive values and should be ignored or replaced by runtime injection.

faq.question: Why is UV included?
faq.answer: UV provides fast Python dependency and environment management, which supports repeatable project setup.

faq.question: What should I verify before publishing this skill?
faq.answer: Replace pipe-to-shell install commands and ensure helper output does not reveal secret values by default.
